Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from Legal before we schedule the follow-up:

1) Controller/Processor: we want explicit language that Acme is the controller for customer-provided PII and Redwood is the processor. Can you confirm Redwood is willing to accept processor obligations in the DPA?

2) Subprocessors: can you confirm whether we get prior notice of new subprocessors and what the opt-out process looks like (if any)? Also, could you confirm whether subprocessor access to PII is audited?

3) Breach notice: what is Redwood's SLA for notifying customers of confirmed incidents involving customer data? We typically request notification within 72 hours for incidents affecting customer PII.

4) Logs & PII: do access logs contain any customer PII (e.g., full text, user identifiers)? What is the default retention period and is longer retention configurable?

5) Data residency: we prefer EU residency for Acme's production data. Does Redwood offer a hosted EU region that guarantees data at rest in the EU? If not, what private / dedicated options exist?

I've attached our redline (legal@acme-payments.com) but happy to take your answers first.

Thanks,

Marissa / Monica — answering Acme's items below so you have a short summary to pass back: 

1) Controller / Processor: Confirmed. Redwood acts as a data processor for customer-supplied content and PII. Our DPA language in section 2.1_ref (attached) reflects processor obligations (data processing only on controller instructions, confidentiality, deletion after termination) and we accept processor liabilities appropriate to the role.

2) Subprocessors: The attached subprocessor_list_2027.csv is the current inventory. We provide notification of new subprocessors via the customer console and email at least 30 days prior to onboarding; customers may object and request migration plans under certain circumstances. Subprocessor access is logged and we include subprocessors in our SOC 2 scope — access reviews occur regularly.

3) Breach notice: Our standard practice is to notify impacted customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that affects customer data; we provide an incident summary, scope, and remediation steps, and follow up with a full report. We also offer contractual SLA tweaks for enterprise contracts as needed.

4) Logs & retention: Access logs include metadata (timestamps, request ids, source IPs) and user identifiers (e.g., account ids). They do not contain full customer PII or message text by default. Default retention for hosted customers is 90 days; for Dedicated/Private customers we can extend retention or provide custom deletion schedules via contract. We can also support targeted deletions on controller request.

5) Data residency: Redwood hosts in multiple regions. Our hosted EU region (Frankfurt / Amsterdam) keeps at-rest encryption keys and data residency within the EU for customers who select EU tenancy. For additional guarantees (e.g., on-prem/VPC), our Private deployment option places the control plane and storage in your VPC/region. We'll loop in Solutions if Acme wants a Dedicated/Private proposal.

Suggested next step: share this summary with Acme and offer a 30-min legal call (GC + Redwood Legal) to walk through redlines. If they provide markups, we can produce a tracked DPA and DocuSign link.

-David
